newsitem.title: USA: Astoria deal signals more consolidation.
newsitem.headline: Astoria deal signals more consolidation.

text.p: Astoria Financial Corp's $293 million deal to buy Greater New York Savings Bank reflects continuing consolidation of banking in the New York City metropolitan area, analysts said.

"I think it's a good fit for Astoria," said analyst Frank Barkocy of Josephthal, Lyon & Ross Inc. He said Greater New York, concentrated in the borough of Brooklyn, has found its revenue growth running into a wall.
The combination of the two thrifts would create an institution with $9.8 billion in assets based on pro-forma financials as of December 31, 1996.

Greater New York was off 1/4 to 17-5/8 in early trading. Barkocy said "most of the price was already reflected last week, with the stock having closed at 17-7/8 Thursday." Greater New York holders would receive $19 per share in cash or stock, subject to certain limitations.

Barkocy said the deal could be "a harbinger of things to come in the New York marketplace." He said other consolidation candidates in the market include Dime Bancorp Inc, GreenPoint Financial Corp, Haven Bancorp Inc and Long Island Bancorp Inc.
Astoria was off 1/4 to 37-5/8 in early trading.
